raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix an illegal memory access / segfault during CUDA graph replay of the standalone draft-model prefill on Blackwell (SM100), reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989#issuecomment-6620438731.

Since #60989, the standalone draft model (`method: "draft_model"`) captures FULL CUDA graphs for its prefill. That prefill is a uniform batch of `num_speculative_tokens + 2` tokens per request, because it adds a correction token. That is one token more than FlashInfer's `reorder_batch_threshold` (`1 + num_speculative_tokens`). The builder therefore classifies every request as a prefill and, on SM100, takes the TRTLLM prefill path.

On that path, `build()` allocated `cum_seq_lens_q` as a new tensor (`qo_indptr[prefill_start:] - qo_indptr[prefill_start]`). Attention metadata is built outside the graph, so a FULL graph keeps the address that tensor had at capture time. The tensor is freed after capture and its memory is reused. At replay, the attention kernel reads query offsets from that reused memory. The result is wrong drafts or, for large batches, `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` or a segfault in `cuGraphLaunch`.

This PR writes the offsets into a persistent buffer owned by the builder, the same way `paged_kv_indptr` already works, so every build updates the memory the graph reads. The other tensors on this path (`seq_lens`, `block_tables`, `cum_seq_lens_kv`) are already views of persistent buffers.

Not covered here: with an FP8 KV cache and a non-FP8 query, the same path also makes a contiguous copy of `block_tables` on each build, which would have the same problem under a FULL graph. That configuration was not tested, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_cudagraph.py`. It builds TRTLLM prefill metadata twice, for uniform batches wider than the reorder threshold, and checks that `cum_seq_lens_q` holds the right offsets and stays at the same address.
- End to end on 1x GB200 with model runner V2:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 256 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --seed 0
# and again with --max-concurrency 32
```

## Test Result

- Unit test: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `cum_seq_lens_q moved between builds`.
- GSM8K end to end (1319 questions, greedy decoding; target Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, K=3):

| Setup | C256 | C32 | Mean accepted tokens per draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform decode graphs up to 256 requests (as in #63406), without this fix | crash (illegal memory access) | n/a | n/a |
| Same, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, attention runs eagerly (reference) | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |
| main, with this fix | 0.886 | 0.886 | 2.44 |

On main without this fix, the crash is intermittent: graphs there stop at about 200 requests, so a crash depends on what the freed memory holds. With the fix, accuracy and acceptance match the PIECEWISE reference, which shows the replayed draft prefill now reads the correct query offsets.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""FlashInfer GQA builder: TRTLLM prefill metadata must be CUDA-graph safe."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+    pytest.skip("FlashInfer backend requires a CUDA platform.", allow_module_level=True)
+
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends import flashinfer as flashinfer_backend
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flashinfer import (
+    FlashInferMetadataBuilder,
+    TRTLLMPrefill,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import PerLayerParameters
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import FullAttentionSpec
+
+
+def test_trtllm_prefill_query_offsets_use_a_persistent_buffer(monkeypatch):
+    """A uniform batch wider than reorder_batch_threshold (e.g. the draft-model
+    prefill, num_speculative_tokens + 2 tokens per request) takes the TRTLLM
+    prefill path and can be captured in a FULL CUDA graph. The graph keeps the
+    address of cum_seq_lens_q from capture time, so every build must write the
+    offsets into the same buffer instead of allocating a new tensor.
+    """
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(max_model_len=1024, max_num_seqs=8)
+    vllm_config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+        method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=3
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        flashinfer_backend, "use_trtllm_attention", lambda *args, **kwargs: True
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        flashinfer_backend,
+        "get_per_layer_parameters",
+        lambda *args, **kwargs: {
+            "layer.0": PerLayerParameters(
+                window_left=-1, logits_soft_cap=None, sm_scale=0.1, has_sinks=False
+            )
+        },
+    )
+
+    block_size = 16
+    kv_cache_spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_kv_heads=vllm_config.model_config.get_num_kv_heads(
+            vllm_config.parallel_config
+        ),
+        head_size=vllm_config.model_config.get_head_size(),
+        dtype=vllm_config.model_config.dtype,
+    )
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        builder = FlashInferMetadataBuilder(
+            kv_cache_spec, ["layer.0"], vllm_config, device
+        )
+    query_len = builder.reorder_batch_threshold + 1
+
+    # Keep every build's offsets alive so a fresh allocation cannot reuse the
+    # previous address.
+    offsets = []
+    for num_reqs in (4, 3):
+        common = create_common_attn_metadata(
+            BatchSpec(seq_lens=[64] * num_reqs, query_lens=[query_len] * num_reqs),
+            block_size,
+            device,
+        )
+        metadata = builder.build(0, common)
+        assert metadata.num_decodes == 0
+        assert isinstance(metadata.prefill, TRTLLMPrefill)
+        cum_seq_lens_q = metadata.prefill.cum_seq_lens_q
+        expected = torch.arange(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32) * query_len
+        torch.testing.assert_close(cum_seq_lens_q.cpu(), expected)
+        offsets.append(cum_seq_lens_q)
+    pointers = {t.data_ptr() for t in offsets}
+    assert len(pointers) == 1, "cum_seq_lens_q moved between builds"

@@ -1126,6 +1126,13 @@ def __init__(
         self.paged_kv_last_page_len = CpuGpuBuffer(
             max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device, pin_memory=False
         )
+        # Rebased query offsets for TRTLLM prefill. Persistent because a FULL
+        # CUDA graph can capture this path (e.g. a draft-model prefill whose
+        # uniform query length exceeds reorder_batch_threshold) and keeps the
+        # address it saw at capture time.
+        self.qo_indptr_prefill = torch.zeros(
+            max_num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+        )
 
     def _resolve_cache_dtype(self) -> str:
         cache_dtype = self.cache_config.cache_dtype
@@ -1768,8 +1775,13 @@ def build(
                 # use_trtllm_attention never selects it when DCP is enabled.
                 assert not self.use_dcp
                 # Create GPU versions
-                qo_indptr_prefill_gpu = (
-                    qo_indptr[prefill_start:] - qo_indptr[prefill_start]
+                qo_indptr_prefill_gpu = self.qo_indptr_prefill[
+                    : num_reqs + 1 - prefill_start
+                ]
+                torch.sub(
+                    qo_indptr[prefill_start : num_reqs + 1],
+                    qo_indptr[prefill_start],
+                    out=qo_indptr_prefill_gpu,
                 )
                 # Compute cum_seq_lens_kv on GPU to avoid CPU sync.
                 # This is the cumulative sum of the number of KV cache
